fixes.what: Change `align-content:center` to `align-content:end` and add `padding-bottom:clamp(40px, 6vh, 80px)` on `.screen--statement .screen__col` at desktop widths.
fixes.why: On desktop (shot 1), the canopy fills the top ~65% of the viewport, pushing the 'Reimagined Heritage' heading down to the bottom edge while the statement and three promises sit completely off-screen below the fold until the user scrolls past the canopy.

fixes.what: Promote the 'Afghan weddings · عروسی افغان' `.seasonal` callout or mention Afghan traditions (like Aina Mosaf / Shirni-khori) in the first sentence of the `#nikah` section, and link 'Aina Mosaf' in the `.jump` nav.
fixes.why: Afghan families are one of the three core audiences named in the hero, yet they have no top-level ceremony heading or jump link on the Weddings page and must read halfway through the Nikah section to see themselves explicitly named.

fixes.what: Change the Message textarea placeholder from `'Your families, your dates, the rituals that matter most.'` to `'Your families, approximate dates and guest count, Bay Area location, and the rituals that matter most.'`
fixes.why: In Persian, Afghan, and South Asian multi-day weddings, guest count (often 250–600+) and sub-region (Peninsula vs. East Bay vs. South Bay) immediately dictate venue viability and scope; prompting for them upfront makes the first reply far more actionable.
